# Freeze store integrity maintenance

Ensure the `TextFileBasedViolationStore` maintains the integrity of its `stored.rules` index and files.

Setting `default.integrity` to `repair` will check the index and folder as they are on disk during initialization, even if the same folder was initialized before. Defaulting to `ignore` which checks nothing.

If an entry points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the folder, it is broken. This also applies if the file name is not a valid path.

If an entry is not broken and its file has no violations it is resolved. Files that only contain line breaks are also resolved.

Entries that point to the same file name are shared, even if nothing exists with that name. If multiple entries point to the same file they are also shared. Including through a symbolic or hard link. Even if that file is outside the folder.

The `TextFileBasedViolationStore` will not touch any shared entries or files that no entry points to. If an entry is shared and anything else it will remain shared.

When set to `repair` broken entries will be discarded.

When set to `repair` resolved entries and the file they point to will be discarded. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link the file it points to will be deleted as well.

If using `repair` and saving no violations for a known rule it will forget the rule. Its entry will be removed and its file as well. Unless another entry is sharing that file. In which case only the entry will be removed. Even if it points outside the folder. If using `repair` and saving no violations for an unknown rule nothing will be saved.

If it cannot delete the file of a rule it is forgetting it will fail to save and leave the entry.

### Summary of Changes

To maintain the integrity of the violation store's index and files, the following changes were implemented in [`TextFileBasedViolationStore`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java):

1. **Integrity Configuration (`default.integrity`)**:
   - Added configuration property `default.integrity` defaulting to `ignore` (which checks nothing) and accepting `repair`.
   - When set to `repair`, the store inspects the index (`stored.rules`) and folder as they are on disk upon initialization, reloading and checking even if the same folder was initialized previously.

2. **Entry Classification & Integrity Checks**:
   - **Shared entries**: Entries pointing to the same file name (even if the file does not exist) or pointing to the same file (including hard links and symbolic links, even outside the store folder) are identified as shared. If an entry is shared, it remains shared and [`TextFileBasedViolationStore`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java) will not touch it or any files that no entry points to.
   - **Broken entries**: An unshared entry is broken if its file name is not a valid path or points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the folder (e.g. non-existent, directories, subdirectories, path traversal `..`, or broken symbolic links). When set to `repair`, broken entries are discarded from `stored.rules`.
   - **Resolved entries**: An unshared entry that is not broken and whose file contains no violations (empty or containing only line breaks `\n` / `\r\n`) is resolved. When set to `repair`, the resolved entry and its file are discarded. If the entry is a symbolic link, both the symbolic link and the file it points to are deleted.

3. **Saving Violations with `repair`**:
   - Saving no violations for an **unknown rule** saves nothing (no files created, no entries added).
   - Saving no violations for a **known rule** forgets the rule: its entry is removed and its file is deleted (including if pointing outside the folder, or deleting both link and target if a symbolic link), unless another entry is sharing that file (in which case only the entry is removed).
   - If deleting the file fails, `save` fails with a [`StoreUpdateFailedException`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/StoreUpdateFailedException.java) and leaves the entry in `stored.rules`.

4. **Exception Handling**:
   - Added a `(String message, Throwable cause)` constructor to [`StoreUpdateFailedException`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/StoreUpdateFailedException.java) for preserving root causes when deletion or file sync fails.

---

### Verification

Comprehensive unit tests were added in [`TextFileBasedViolationStoreIntegrityTest`](file:///app/archunit/src/test/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStoreIntegrityTest.java) to verify all requirements:
- `default.integrity` defaulting to `ignore` and checking nothing.
- Discarding broken entries (non-existent, directories, paths outside folder, subfolders, invalid path characters, broken symlinks, symlinks to directories) without deleting non-entry targets.
- Discarding resolved entries (0-byte files, files with only Unix or CRLF line breaks) and deleting their files while keeping entries with violations.
- Deleting both symbolic link and target file when a resolved entry is a symbolic link.
- Preserving shared entries (same name, hard links, symbolic links to same target, symlink pointing to target entry, shared files outside folder) even if broken or resolved.
- Preserving unreferenced files in the folder.
- Re-checking on-disk state when initializing a folder that was previously initialized.
- Saving no violations for unknown rules saving nothing.
- Saving no violations for known rules forgetting the rule and deleting the file.
- Saving no violations for shared rules removing only the entry while preserving the file until no longer shared.
- Leaving the entry intact and raising [`StoreUpdateFailedException`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/StoreUpdateFailedException.java) when deleting the violation file fails.
